## Responding to LLM-Review -1 on change 2278

### BLOCKER 1 — stale prose contradicting the retyped field: FIXED, and the sweep went wider

The reviewer found `src/rebar/schemas/sign_result.schema.json:5`, whose top-level `description`
still said *"signed_at is a ns-epoch integer"* while the property itself was already
`["integer", "string"]`. A published schema contradicting itself about the wire type of the very
field the change retypes is worse than one that says nothing. Corrected to name both forms and
point at the property for the full contract.

The instruction was to assume more existed and prove otherwise, so I did not sweep by keyword
guess. I walked **every** `description`, `title` and `$comment` string in **all 24 schemas**
programmatically, flagging any prose that names one of the six affected fields *and* asserts an
integer/number type. Then I extended the same sweep to `docs/`, `src/` (including MCP tool
docstrings, which are published to clients as tool descriptions), `templates/`, `examples/`,
`.agents/`, `AGENTS.md` and `CONTRIBUTING.md`.

**That found a second real instance the reviewer did not flag:**
`examples/agent-skills/rebar-debug/SKILL.md:184` told agents *"`created_at` is an integer of
**nanoseconds**"* — in the packaged debugging skill, in the Step 0(b) instruction that divides
`created_at` by 1e9 to date a bug report. An agent following it against the MCP surface would now
be reading a string. Corrected to state both forms and to coerce with `int()`.

Two further candidates were checked and are **not** stale, recorded so the next reader does not
re-open them: `docs/event-schema.md:52` lists the SIGNATURE **event** field names with no type
claim (the event log is unchanged by this fix — the store still holds integers), and
`_mcp_reads.py:178` / `_mcp_writes.py:483` name `signed_at` without asserting a type.

Final sweep result: **0 remaining claims of that shape, repo-wide.**

### ADVISORY 1 — the vacuous test: FIXED, and proven to bite

`test_list_tickets_emits_no_uninteroperable_integer` asserted only `not hits`, which passes on an
empty list, an error envelope, or a payload with no timestamps — the same failure mode as a skipped
test reading as green. It now anchors liveness **before** the absence assertion is allowed to mean
anything: real ticket rows returned, the ticket under test present in the listing, `created_at` and
`updated_at` actually on the row, and the value genuinely outside the safe range so the guard had
work to do.

Proven, not asserted — mutating the call to return an empty result:

```
AssertionError: list_tickets returned no ticket rows, so this test would pass without
checking anything: {'result': []}
```

The old version would have reported that as green.

### ADVISORY 2 — no wire-level test for the declared-int coercion: FIXED

Three new tests drive `sign_manifest`, `verify_signature` and `plan_review_status` through the
**registered `CallToolRequest` handler** and assert `structuredContent.signed_at` is a decimal
string, that it round-trips losslessly (`verify_signature` must read back the exact instant
`sign_manifest` wrote), and that the `content` text block and `structuredContent` **agree** — the
divergence being the specific symptom that made the original miss insidious. `plan_review_status`
carries the weaker but unconditional assertion (null-or-string, never a bare out-of-range integer),
because populating it needs a live LLM call; that limitation is stated in the test.

Mutation check — reverting the three `signed_at` annotations to bare `int` turns **three** tests
RED, and the new wire tests fail at the right layer with the right message:

```
AssertionError: signed_at reached structuredContent as int (1787869585331218000) —
model_validate coerced the JS-safe string back to a bare out-of-range integer
AssertionError: verify_signature emitted signed_at as int
```

So they exercise the coercion path itself, not merely the schema. The test file is now **8 tests,
all green**.

### BLOCKER 2 — the attestation

`rebar review-plan` was run **locally** (the repo `.venv`, which has the bedrock provider) rather
than through the MCP server, per the note about `facial-lunar-urson`. First run returned **BLOCK**,
with both blocking findings pointing at the same thing: the ticket's **"Likely cause"** section —
the original Copilot-authored guess that a field "is represented as a JS `BigInt` somewhere in the
MCP server's serialization path". The reviewer refused a plan whose stated cause names an edit
target that cannot exist in a Python codebase. **That refusal is correct**, and it is the same
error I documented in my first comment; the ticket body had simply never been corrected to match.

So I improved the plan rather than forcing: the section is now **"Root cause (PROVEN — supersedes
the original 'Likely cause' guess)"**, carrying the mechanism, the `path` citations, the measured
per-tool counts, the two client failure modes, the in-repo precedent, and the fix shape — with an
explicit note that the prior text was wrong and why. All other sections, including the operator's
**LIVE VALIDATION** criterion, are preserved verbatim. Re-review is running; verdict to follow.

### Verification on the amended commit

`make lint` **All checks passed** (`new=0 increased=0`) · `make typecheck` **677 files clean** ·
new test file **8 passed** · `tests/interfaces/contracts` **338 passed** ·
`tests/interfaces/facades` **634 passed, 1 skipped**. Re-confirmed end to end with the real JS MCP
client on the final tree: `list_tickets(open,epic)` 8 tickets and `ready_tickets` 71 tickets both
stringify with no BigInt error.

Commit amended to **`ed650f7c1900e880dc0df5a7c159871b8125760e`** (15 files, +578/−26) via
`make amend-msg`, so `Change-Id: Ibb73ba743c8b99cc9ddd3165c9670bf4fcfd934a` is preserved. Still not
pushed.

### Unrelated observation, recorded not acted on

During this work the tickets-branch auto-push failed repeatedly
(`cannot lock ref 'refs/heads/tickets'`, backlog reaching 16 unpushed commits) because other
sessions were pushing concurrently. It **self-healed** back to 1 without intervention. No raw git
was run against the tracker. Noting it because the warning text ("the backlog GREW since the
previous failure") reads alarming but was transient contention, not data loss.
